items.text: Selection methods · Fetchers · Spiders · Proxy Rotation · CLI · MCP Scrapling is a Python Web Scraping framework that brings fast HTTP requests, stealth browsers, powerful parsing, and concurrent crawling into one library. Scrape static pages, render JavaScript, interact with websites, and extract data from the API calls behind them. Build crawlers with reusable sessions, proxy rotation, automatic retries, pause/resume, and built-in data exports. Use it from Python, the terminal, or your AI agent through its MCP server and Agent Skill. From extracting a few fields to collecting a whole website as clean Markdown, Scrapling covers the full scraping workflow. - Fetch & interact: Fast HTTP requests, stealth browsers, JavaScript rendering, Cloudflare Turnstile/Interstitial handling, persistent sessions, and background API capture. - Parse & extract: CSS, XPath, text and regex search, adaptive element tracking, similar-element matching, and clean Markdown output. - Crawl & export: Concurrent spiders, proxy rotation, retries, AutoThrottle, pause/resume, streaming, ready-made templates, and JSON/JSONL/CSV/XML exports. - Scrape with AI or from your terminal: An MCP server for AI agents to browse and extract data, an Agent Skill, CLI commands, and an interactive shell. Start with a single page: from scrapling.fetchers import Fetcher page = Fetcher.get('https://quotes.toscrape.com/') quotes = page.css('.quote .text::text').getall() print(quotes) Or scale up with a spider: from scrapling.spiders import Spider, Response class QuotesSpider(Spider): name = "quotes" start_urls = ["https://quotes.toscrape.com/"] async def parse(self, response: Response): for quote in response.css('.quote'): yield { "text": quote.css('.text::text').get(), "author": quote.css('.author::text').get(), } res...

items.summary: Agent 上网与调研入口聚合，把网页、视频、社区、仓库交给 Agent 查。
items.text: 让 AI Agent 够得着它自己上不去的互联网 让你的 Agent 直接搜索和阅读 X、Reddit、YouTube、小红书…… 💬 有问题、想要新平台、或者想看看别人怎么用？来 Discord 聊聊。 点击展开 Agent Reach 让你的 Agent 真正连上互联网，用上它自己够不着的平台和能力。 Claude Code、Codex、Hermes Agent、OpenClaw 这类 CLI Agent 自带搜索和网页读取，但下面这些它们基本够不着： - 要登录才能用的功能：在小红书搜笔记、在 X 查账号动态、读职位详情等。 - 视频里的内容：B站和 YouTube 的字幕，以及 YouTube 视频、小宇宙播客的语音转文字。 - 中文平台：B站、小红书、V2EX、雪球，通用搜索覆盖很差。 - 干净的结构化数据：雪球行情、V2EX 帖子和回复、GitHub 仓库和 issue，拿到的是整理好的内容。 Agent Reach 把这些平台背后的工具替你装好、测好，Agent 一条命令就能用： agent-reach channels # 有哪些渠道、每个渠道能做什么 agent-reach bilibili search "大模型" # agent-reach [参数] agent-reach read https://www.v2ex.com/t/123 # 按链接自动选渠道 - 适用于哪些 Agent？ 一切 Agent 都能用。 - 会碰我的浏览器和账号吗？ 要登录的平台用 Agent Reach 自己的专用浏览器，在后台运行、不弹窗。第一次用某个网站时，会把你 Chrome 里这个网站的登录复制一份过去，原浏览器不变，不读密码库。复制过来的通常是主账号，建议换成小号，做法见下面的"安全性"。详见会话配置。 下表是当前版本的情况。 - 默认：装好就能用；不想要也可以去掉，以后更新不会再加回来。 - 可选：说一句"帮我加上 XX"就开启，需要的软件会自动装好。 - 实验：能用，但平台反爬更严，可能随时失效。 把这句话发给你的 Agent： 帮我安装 Agent Reach：https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Panniantong/Agent-Reach/main/docs/install.md 无论是安装还是升级，都只需要这一条命令就行了。 剩下的 Agent 自己做完。过程中你可能会被问到： - 允许它执行命令：如果 Agent 说自己不能运行命令，去它的设置里打开"允许执行命令"。 - 装 uv：uv 是一个安装命令行程序的小工具，不需要管理员密码。电脑上没有的话 Agent 会先装它，会跟你说一声。 - 要不要加可选渠道：装完后 Agent 会告诉你哪些已经能用（B站、V2EX、GitHub、YouTube、网页），以及还能加哪些。你选了再加，也可以以后随时说"帮我加上小红书"，一条命令就装好。 关于登录：部分平台会直接复用你电脑上已有的登录。想换成某个特定账号（比如小号），跟 Agent 说一声就行。Agent 从不替你登录，也不会要你的密码。 ⚠️ PyPI 上叫agent-reach 的包不是本项目，请勿从 PyPI 安装，只用 install.md 里的 GitHub 地址。 Agent Reach 装的所有东西（各渠道的工具、登录、设置）都放在你电脑上同一个文件夹里（~/.agent-reach/ ），不散落到别处。所以升级、管理、删除都很省事，一句话就行。 直接用大白话跟 Agent 说： 出了问题，Agent 会告诉你是哪个平台、什么原因、下一步怎么做。常见问题见 troubleshooting.md。 每个平台的每个动作都有一个按顺序尝试的工具列表。比如读 B站视频先用 bili-cli，失败了自动换 B站公开接口；读网页先用 Jina Reader，再用 Exa。 flowchart LR A[Agent] -->|agent-reach 渠道 动作| B[Agent Reach] B --> C{按顺序尝试} C -->|首选| D[上游工具 1] C -->|失败时备选| E[上游工具 2] D --> F[结果] E --> F F --> A 平台改版、工具失效是...

items.text: 伯乐Skill（Scout Skill）帮你从一堆信源里选出千里马。 AI News Radar 是一个自动更新的 24 小时 AI 更新雷达。 普通用户直接打开网页，看最近 24 小时 AI、模型、开发者工具和技术生态更新。维护者可以 fork 这个仓库，接入自己的 OPML/RSS、公开 feed、静态页面或 AgentMail 邮箱情报。Codex / Claude Code 这类 Agent 可以使用项目内置的 伯乐Skill，继续帮你判断信息源、维护抓取逻辑、部署 GitHub Pages。 这个项目不是“又一个新闻网页”。 它的核心是伯乐Skill，帮你从一堆信源里选出千里马。哪些源值得长期追踪，哪些源适合做成RSS/OPML，哪些源只能接付费的API，哪些源看起来更新很多但实际上跟你长期关注的方面比方AI只占了里面的5%不到。 先判断清楚，再接入。 好新闻分散在各处， 官方博客发一点，更新日志发一点，X 上有人提前爆料，聚合站又把同一个新闻转来转去。 我以为的自己在追前沿，实际每天都在重复三件事， 打开几十个页面，肉眼+人脑过滤重复内容，猜哪条值得看。 伯乐Skill先替你完成第一轮判断，哪些信源是千里马，哪些是噪音。 你可以随意增加信息源，还可以把一个信息源纳入输入范围，先让它在单独的展示区域运行一个月，再判断要不要录入。 AI News Radar从来都不是单纯把信息抓回来， 它更像是一条轻量的新闻pipeline，把来源判断、抓取、去重、AI强相关过滤、信息源健康状态和静态网页发布串起来，上线后不消耗模型额度。 - 追踪官方 AI 节点，OpenAI News、OpenAI Codex Changelog、OpenAI Skills、Anthropic、Google DeepMind、Google AI、Hugging Face、GitHub AI 等 - 读取高信号日报和Newsletter公开来源，例如 AI Breakfast - 读取网页自带的feed，例如 Follow Builders 的 X builders、Anthropic Engineering、Claude Blog、AI podcasts - 同时接入多个公开聚合源，例如 AI HOT，补足普通官方源看不到的盲区 - 支持OPML/RSS批量导入 - 支持AgentMail邮箱订阅高质量AI日报 - 输出24小时双视图， AI强相关 和全量 - 中英双语标题和站点分组 - 兼容飞书文档，追加了WaytoAGI开源社区最近更新日和近7日变化 flowchart LR source["信息源清单"] --> classify["伯乐Skill判断信源类型"] classify --> official["官方 RSS / changelog"] classify --> opml["私人 OPML / RSS"] classify --> publicFeed["公开 GitHub feed / JSON"] classify --> staticPage["公开页面 / Jina 兜底"] classify --> privateMail["AgentMail 邮箱订阅"] classify --> skip["跳过高风险来源"] official --> fetch["抓取与结构化"] opml --> fetch publicFeed --> fetch staticPage --> fetch privateMail --> fetch fetch --> dedup["去重与归一化"] dedup --> filter["AI 强相关过滤"] filter --> status["源健康与覆盖统计"] filter --> data["data/*.json"] status --> data data --> pages["GitHub Pages 网页"] data --> agent["Codex / Claude Code 继续维护"] AI News Radar学习了现代新闻学的技术，不是简单堆信息源，一次性放几万条信息出来等于没用，所以我选择把新闻处理拆成稳定pipeline，抓取，去重，过滤，补充状态，生成静态站点。 在...

items.title: Inkling 2 Small
items.summary: Comments
items.text: Today we are introducing our second model generation with Inkling 2 Small. It is a Mixture-of-Experts model with 594B total parameters, 17B active, and supports image inputs and variable effort. Inkling 2 Small far surpasses our previous models’ scores on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with a score of 31, reflecting gains in performance on agentic coding, vision, knowledge work, and reasoning. The increase in capabilities comes from improvements made at every step of our training process, including more efficient pre-training and a large, unified RL run. Inkling 2 Small will initially be available through Tinker, with closed weights, following the approach we outlined in a safe path to open weights. We intend to make the full weights available under an Apache 2.0 license next week after the completion of external safety testing and red-teaming. You can try Inkling 2 Small on Tinker Playground today. The model is also available for fine-tuning and sampling on Tinker; checkpoints will be downloadable with the release of Inkling 2 Small’s weights. Capabilities Inkling 2 Small is more capable across the board than our first generation, particularly in long-horizon autonomous work. Inkling 2 Small’s vision and agentic capabilities enable it to incorporate visual feedback to iteratively build and refine websites, games, and 3D designs with interactive elements. Agentic coding and autoresearch Inkling 2 Small was trained with RL on hundreds of thousands of long-horizon coding tasks across multiple agent harnesses and context-compaction strategies. items.title: datasette-apps 0.3a0
items.summary: Release: datasette-apps 0.3a0 Datasette Apps adds support for hosting and editing custom HTML applications inside of Datasette. These can be created by hand, but it's easier to create them using LLMs via Datasette Agent . This release improves that integration: Apps can now be tagged in Datasette Agent chat messages by typing # , which autocompletes from the apps the user has permission to view. New app_add_stored_queries() and app_remove_stored_queries() tools let the agent manage which stored queries an app is allowed to call. Granting a write query requires approval from the user first. app_create() now checks that each requested stored query exists and that the user can view it, and asks the user to approve any write queries before the app is created. The "View app" buttons shown by the agent tools, and the links on # app references, now open the app full screen in the Datasette Agent panel. Tags: datasette , datasette-agent , datasette-apps

items.title: GitHub Universe 2026: Evolving every layer of the stack
items.summary: Today, we laid out our vision for GitHub as the most comprehensive, end-to-end software delivery system in the world. The post GitHub Universe 2026: Evolving every layer of the stack appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
items.text: Our jobs as developers are changing. In a couple of years, we’ve gone from writing every line of code to working with AI assistants to orchestrating fleets of agents. But the goal hasn’t changed: ship completed software work. A feature, a bug fix, a security fix. Completed work, not more code, is the output that matters. Today at GitHub Universe, we shared our vision for GitHub as the most comprehensive software delivery system in the world. We introduced products that bring that vision to life and showed how we’re rebuilding the infrastructure underneath it. Our vision: From idea to completed software The SDLC is no longer a linear path from planning to coding to testing to deployment. A code change, a request from a colleague, or a production metric can trigger work anywhere in the system. Most of us (and our agents) jump between different stages, depending on the task at hand. Developers set the direction, make decisions, and stay accountable for what ships. Agents implement and verify changes. And everything feeds into and out of a continuous learning machine that makes the next cycle better. This agentic software delivery system solves for three things: - Velocity: get from idea to completed software as quickly, efficiently, and cost-effectively as possible - Intelligence: combine context across the platform with a continuous learning engine, so the system gets better as you use it - Quality: make completed work secure by default and catch bugs before they ship GitHub is built for developers and their agents. A "Hackintosh" is the feat of running macOS on non-Apple hardware, and has a history dating back to the late 1980s. At the time KVM and PCI passthrough were relatively new technologies, and this guide provided near-native performance with GPU acceleration. A few years passed by, and we saw Apple release the first ARM-based Mac in 2021, the M1 MacBook Air. The timing was impeccable, Intel was unable to create competitive processors (due to being stuck on the 14nm node), and Apple had powerful and efficient ARM chips already being shipped in their iPhones. The long battery life, the fanless design, the instant wake, what's not to like? The benefits of switching to ARM were clear, however to most, this was thought to be the final chapter in the hackintosh community. x86 versions of macOS would soon be discontinued, and the hackintosh community would slowly fade away. That day has come and the latest version of macOS 27 (Golden Gate) released this year is no longer compatible with x86... Just a few days ago, I decided to create an iOS app for the first time. After some initial tinkering with x86 workarounds, I was pleased that I had a functional iOS app within a day, without touching a single line of code! So how does this all tie in? items.title: Inside GitHub’s new Git storage architecture
items.summary: GitHub's new Git storage architecture is built so thousands of agents can push to a single repository at once. Here's how it works. The post Inside GitHub’s new Git storage architecture appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
items.text: Distinguished Engineer Last week at GitHub Universe, we announced our new Git storage architecture, capable of handling thousands of writes per second with reads that scale on demand. Through internal testing, we’ve demonstrated the ability to support 5,000 concurrent agents working on a repository, sending 7,200 pushes per second to a repo, all while serving read traffic with consistently low latency. This new architecture is the foundation for GitHub to support agentic development for hundreds of millions of developers, and we’ve been building it underneath GitHub while it keeps running. Over the past year, agents changed what a busy repository looks like on GitHub. In our first post in this series, we laid out the two principles behind our next-generation Git storage architecture: minimize coordination, and decouple storage from compute. In our last post, we covered the bridge: moving 99.99999% of repositories into Azure, scoping the write quorum to individual references, and standing up virtual replicas backed by Azure Blob Storage. We also left off with an observation: very little of a write needs to be ordered. Git objects are immutable and named by their contents, meaning two writers can store them at the same time without agreeing on anything. The part of a push that needs agreement is the reference update, and a reference update is tiny in comparison. Virtual replicas were the first step toward building around that, and the means by which we onboard repositories to the new architecture. The rest of the architecture builds on that observation. Only reference updates need agreement. That lets the parts of Git infrastructure that used to be tightly coupled (storing data, serving requests, and maintaining repositories) scale independently. items.title: Alpine Linux Security Advisory: OpenSSH-server password authentication bypass
items.summary: Comments
items.text: Security advisory: openssh-server password authentication bypass If you run sshd on Alpine Linux, update openssh now and restart sshd . Upgrading the package alone does not replace the running daemon. If you cannot update yet, at least disable password logins: set PasswordAuthentication no in your sshd configuration and restart sshd . Either one closes the hole. What is the problem? An attacker who can reach your SSH port can log in without knowing any password. It takes one connection, works every time, and needs no retries. The attacker needs the name of an account whose password field is * (an account with no password set, which is normal for key-only accounts), and needs the machine to have at least one other account with a $5$ or $6$ password hash. The attacker then sends a very long password (257 to 1024 bytes). One user with a password is enough: it makes every account without one reachable. Details are in the OpenSSH 10.6p2 release notes. No CVE identifier had been assigned at the time of writing. Who is affected? You are affected if all of the following are true: - You run the Alpine openssh-server package, which is built without PAM, or you runopenssh-server-pam withUsePAM no . (openssh-server-pam withUsePAM yes is not affected.) PasswordAuthentication isyes (the OpenSSH default, unless you changed it).- The machine has an account whose password field is * . This includes:root , which ships asroot:* in the base image since about Alpine 3.16. OpenSSH’s defaultPermitRootLogin prohibit-password protects root, so root is only reachable ifPermitRootLogin yes is set. That does not help if another account that can log in is able to become root, for example throughdoas .- Any key-only user created with adduser without a password, or withusermod -p '*' . - Users coming...
